caption: The drawing depicts a single, greyish-brown, oval-shaped ceramic vessel placed centrally on a plain, off-white background. The vessel has a smooth, matte exterior with two small, horizontal protruding handles on either side. Its rim is uneven and slightly wavy, with some dents and irregularities visible on the upper edge. The interior of the vessel is brownish, with darker shading suggestive of depth and curvature. Blue floral or foliate patterns are painted on the vessel’s side, including a four-petaled motif and a swirling leaf-like shape. Near the left edge of the vessel, a small, faint red mark is present on the background. There is a handwritten inscription below the vessel that reads “Henrietta Hukill Del-558.” The overall composition is simple, with the vessel occupying the majority of the image space and no other objects present.
title: Stone Cream Crock
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
